questions.question: Electromagnetic induction is the process by which an e.m.f. is induced in a conductor when there is a change in the
options: Magnetic flux linked with the conductor
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction is the process by which an electromotive force (e.m.f.) is induced in a conductor whenever there is a change in the magnetic flux linked with the conductor. This is the principle behind generators and transformers.

questions.question: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the magnitude of the induced e.m.f. is directly proportional to the
options: Rate of change of magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Faraday's law: the induced e.m.f. is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux. Mathematically, E = −N(dΦ/dt).

questions.question: Lenz's law states that the direction of the induced current is such as to
options: Have no effect on the change producing it
questions.explanation: Lenz's law: the induced current flows in such a direction as to oppose the change producing it. This explains the negative sign in Faraday's law.

questions.question: Lenz's law is a consequence of the law of conservation of
questions.explanation: Lenz's law is a direct consequence of the law of conservation of energy. If the induced current aided the change, energy would be created from nothing.

questions.question: The induced e.m.f. in a coil of N turns is given by
questions.explanation: Faraday's law for a coil of N turns: E = N(dΦ/dt), where dΦ/dt is the rate of change of magnetic flux.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of magnetic flux is the
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux is measured in the weber (Wb). One weber is the flux that produces an e.m.f. of 1 V when it changes uniformly in 1 s.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of inductance is the
questions.explanation: Inductance is measured in the henry (H). One henry is the inductance when a current changing at 1 A/s induces an e.m.f. of 1 V.

questions.question: The self-inductance of a coil is defined as the ratio of the
options: Magnetic flux linked to the current producing it
Induced e.m.f. to the rate of change of current
questions.explanation: Self-inductance L is defined as the ratio of the magnetic flux linkage (NΦ) to the current I producing it: L = NΦ/I.

questions.question: The e.m.f. induced in a coil of self-inductance L when the current changes at a rate dI/dt is
questions.explanation: The self-induced e.m.f. is E = L(dI/dt), where L is the self-inductance and dI/dt is the rate of change of current.

questions.question: The energy stored in an inductor of inductance L carrying current I is
questions.explanation: The magnetic energy stored in an inductor is E = ½LI2.

Mutual inductance is the property of two coils by which an e.m.f. is induced in one coil when there is a change in the
questions.explanation: Mutual inductance is the property by which a change in the current in one coil induces an e.m.f. in an adjacent coil.

questions.question: The mutual inductance of two coils depends on
options: The number of turns in each coil, their relative position and the medium
Only the current in the primary coil
Only the resistance of the coils
questions.explanation: Mutual inductance depends on the number of turns in each coil, their relative position, and the permeability of the medium between them.

questions.question: A transformer works on the principle of
questions.explanation: A transformer works on the principle of mutual induction — a changing current in the primary coil induces an e.m.f. in the secondary coil.

questions.question: The ratio of the secondary voltage to the primary voltage in a transformer is equal to the ratio of the
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, where N is the number of turns.

questions.question: A transformer has 4000 turns in its primary and 200 turns in its secondary. If the primary voltage is 240V, the secondary voltage is
questions.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np ⇒ Vs = 240 × (200/4000) = 240 × 0.05 = 12 V.

questions.question: A step-up transformer has
options: More turns in the primary than the secondary
More turns in the secondary than the primary
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer increases voltage, so it has more turns in the secondary than the primary.

questions.question: A step-down transformer has
options: More turns in the primary than the secondary
More turns in the secondary than the primary
questions.explanation: A step-down transformer decreases voltage, so it has more turns in the primary than the secondary.

questions.question: Energy losses in a transformer can be reduced by
options: Using thick copper wires for the windings
questions.explanation: Energy losses are reduced by: (1) thick copper wires — reduces I2R losses; (2) laminated soft iron core — reduces eddy currents; (3) soft iron core — improves flux linkage. So all of the above are correct.

questions.question: Eddy currents in a transformer core are reduced by
questions.explanation: Laminating the core breaks up eddy current paths, reducing energy losses.

questions.question: In a transformer, the efficiency is given by
questions.explanation: Efficiency = (useful power output / power input) × 100%.

questions.question: A transformer has a primary voltage of 240V and a secondary voltage of 12V. If the secondary current is 5A and the transformer is 100% efficient, the primary current is
questions.explanation: For 100% efficiency: VpIp = VsIs ⇒ 240 × Ip = 12 × 5 = 60 ⇒ Ip = 60/240 = 0.25 A.

questions.question: The device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction is the
questions.explanation: A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy via electromagnetic induction.

questions.question: In an a.c. generator, the e.m.f. is maximum when the plane of the coil is
questions.explanation: The e.m.f. is maximum when the coil plane is parallel to the field, because the rate of change of flux is maximum (flux is zero).

questions.question: In an a.c. generator, the e.m.f. is zero when the plane of the coil is
questions.explanation: The e.m.f. is zero when the coil plane is perpendicular to the field, because the flux is maximum but not changing.

questions.question: The peak value of an alternating current is I<sub>0</sub>. The root-mean-square (r.m.s.) value is
questions.explanation: The r.m.s. value of an alternating quantity is the peak value divided by √2: Irms = I0/√2.

questions.question: The r.m.s. value of an alternating current is also known as the
questions.explanation: The r.m.s. value is also called the effective value because it produces the same heating effect as a direct current.

questions.question: An alternating current has a peak value of 10A. Its r.m.s. value is approximately
The r.m.s. value of an a.c. voltage of peak value 311V is approximately
questions.explanation: Vrms = V0/√2 = 311/1.414 = 220 V (the standard mains voltage).

questions.question: In a purely resistive a.c. circuit, the current and voltage are
questions.explanation: In a purely resistive circuit, current and voltage are in phase (phase difference = 0°).

questions.question: In a purely inductive a.c. circuit, the current
options: Is in phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: In a purely inductive circuit, current lags the voltage by 90°.

questions.question: In a purely capacitive a.c. circuit, the current
options: Is in phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: In a purely capacitive circuit, current leads the voltage by 90°.

questions.question: The inductive reactance of a coil is given by
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance is XL = 2πfL, where f is frequency and L is inductance.

questions.question: The capacitive reactance of a capacitor is given by
questions.explanation: Capacitive reactance is XC = 1/(2πfC).

questions.question: The S.I. unit of reactance is the
questions.explanation: Reactance, like resistance, is measured in ohms (Ω).

questions.explanation: Impedance of a series RLC circuit is Z = √(R2 + (XL − XC)2).

questions.question: A series circuit has a resistance of 4Ω and an inductive reactance of 3Ω. Calculate the impedance.
Resonance occurs in a series R-L-C circuit when
questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance: XL = XC.

questions.question: At resonance in a series R-L-C circuit, the impedance is
questions.explanation: At resonance, XL − XC = 0, so Z = R. Impedance is minimum and equal to R.

questions.question: At resonance in a series R-L-C circuit, the current is
questions.explanation: Since impedance is minimum (= R) at resonance, the current is maximum.

questions.question: The resonant frequency of a series R-L-C circuit is given by
questions.explanation: Resonant frequency: fr = 1/(2π√(LC)).

questions.question: At resonance in an a.c. circuit, the phase angle between current and voltage is
questions.explanation: At resonance, the circuit behaves as purely resistive, so the phase angle is 0°.

questions.question: The power factor of an a.c. circuit is given by
questions.explanation: The power factor is cosφ, where φ is the phase angle between current and voltage.

questions.question: In a purely inductive or purely capacitive a.c. circuit, the power factor is
questions.explanation: In purely inductive or capacitive circuits, φ = 90°, so cosφ = 0.

questions.question: The average power consumed in a purely resistive a.c. circuit is given by
questions.explanation: Average power in a resistive circuit: P = IrmsVrms = Irms2R. So both A and B are correct.

options: Equal in magnitude and opposite in phase
Equal in magnitude and in phase
questions.explanation: At resonance, VL and VC are equal in magnitude and opposite in phase, so they cancel each other.
